e: Syria confirms sending soldiers to Saudi Arabia to defending the country from the Houthis.
The defence ministries of Saudi Arabia and Syria sign a cooperation pact.
Authorities state that they thwarted a Hezbollah-connected plot to attack the Homs oil refinery.
The Jordanian Armed Forces announces that it stopped 14 armed individuals who were trying to cross the northern border from Syria, adding that it had inflicted multiple casualties during a firefight.
Five people, including four children are killed in flash floods in several governorates.
Jordan and Syria decide to form a joint investigative committee following the Jordanian strikes against Islamic State militants in Syria.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi arrives in Damascus to meet with President al-Sharaa, marking the first visit of an Iraqi prime minister to Syria since the fall of the Assad regime.

Jordan announces that it carried out attacks against militant hideouts in Daraa Governorate in response to a deadly church attack blamed on organizations operating there. However, Syria announces that eight people, including three children and an elderly man, were killed in the attacks. Syria later shuts the Nasib Border Crossing. Jordan claims that the strikes killed 20 Islamic State militants, but also admitted civilian casualties.
Hundreds of Syrians demonstrate against IDF operations on their soil.
Authorities announce that two members of the security forces were killed in an operation targeting a cell connected with the Islamic State in Rankous.
Syria and the World Bank agree to establish a fund for recovery and reconstruction.
Two supporters of former President Bashar al-Assad are sentenced to death by an Aleppo court for inciting an uprising last year.
Syria signs a framework agreement with Eagle Hills Properties for two major property development projects.
Authorities announce that they detained a cell connected to Hezbollah who were preparing rocket launchers from Yarmuk basin in Daraa Governorate, a claim denied by Hezbollah.
Syria is removed from the US munitions export prohibition list.
Three power plants are out of service following an explosion at the Tishreen plant.
At least seven people are killed in a gun attack on a bus in Homs.
Amid the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iraq starts importing gasoline through the port of Baniyas.
Fourteen Israeli settlement activists are arrested by the IDF after crossing into the country.
At least four people are wounded in a blast at an arms depot in an army facility near Al-Eiss.
Authorities announce the arrest of the leader of a militant cell involved in the killing of security personnel while they were trying to arrest an Islamic State militant in As-Sanamayn.
Eleven people are killed in a blast at a military site in Deir ez-Zor Governorate.
Singer Assala performs in the country after a 15-year exile.
Former Adra Prison director and Deir ez-Zor governor Samir Ousman Alsheikh is sentenced to 60 years in prison in the United States for torturing detainees while running Adra Prison from 2005 to 2008.
Syria abolishes the Counter-Terrorism Court established by the Assad regime in 2012.
Fuel price increases spark largest protests since the fall of the Assad regime throughout the country.
A boy is killed in an unexploded ordnance explosion in the vicinity of Damascus.
At least seven people are killed in a jail riot and fire in Kobani.
Authorities announce the arrest of nine former pilots for alleged involvement in the shelling of rebel-held areas during the civil war.
Fourteen people are killed and 11 others are injured in an explosion at an arms depot in the vicinity of Sarmada.
The Syria noncompliance complaint is lifted by the IAEA.
Syria's UN envoy states that the country has begun to destroy chemical weapons materials from the Assad era.

Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert confirms for the first time that Israel was behind the 2008 assassination of Assad's top military adviser, Muhammad Suleiman, due to his responsibility in the construction and security of a Syrian nuclear facility in Deir ez-Zor that Israel struck in 2007.
The IAEA announces that a Syrian site attacked by Israel in 2007 is "consistent with nuclear reactor", adding that the Assad regime “failed to report nuclear material, facilities and activities.”
Two civilians are killed by government shelling in Suwayda.
A soldier who served under the Assad regime is killed after opening fire on security forces who attempt to arrest him.
Druze militias in As-Suwayda Governorate prevent students from traveling to take official exams, demanding that they be held instead in areas under their control, citing security concerns.
Intermittent clashes break out between Druze spiritual leader Hikmat al-Hijri's armed group and government forces in Suwayda.
Mazloum Abdi is appointed by president al-Sharaa as a presidential adviser, while the education ministry issues a decision allowing Kurdish-language instruction in public and private schools.
Mazloum Abdi, the head of the Syrian Democratic Forces, announces the group’s dissolution.
